context: Reorderable adjacency matrix showing a 35-node, 5-community network with ~200 weighted edges; includes a synchronized degree bar chart on the right, three ordering modes (name, degree, community), hover highlighting, and a tooltip.
first_impression: Clean and well-composed at first glance, but the default name-ordered view scatters community structure across the matrix, hiding the primary insight until the user clicks Community.
what_works: The 5-color Tol Bright palette is perceptually well-chosen and used consistently across labels, bars, and legend, making community membership immediately readable; the synchronized degree bar chart adds meaningful context without cluttering the main view.
what_doesnt: The default Name ordering is the worst possible starting view for a community-structure visualization — the blocks are invisible and the subtitle hints at reordering but users may not act on it; at 35 nodes the rotated column labels (~15px cell width) are near the minimum legible size and would break at any viewport narrower than the design width.
